text:
tess: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing we formalize a control-plane demarcation at the customer VPC edge instead of consolidating everything on a regional transit gateway. sketching tradeoffs and a rollout concept, want quick takes before i turn this into an RFC revision.

kevin: tl;dr? what operational delta are we signing up for?

maria: TGW consolidation: fewer peering objects, simpler central billing, easier to reason about egress throughput. downside = larger blast radius, srcIP semantics lost if we NAT, and more complex per-tenant auditing. edge demarcation: more attachments and route table growth, but better isolation, srcIP preservation, and easier compliance for regulated tenants.

sam: preserving srcIP is a big customer ask for firewall allowlists. if we NAT behind TGW customers flip out. also debugging (traceroutes, conntrack) is easier with preserved src.

kevin: do we hit AWS limits quickly if we go edge-per-tenant? attachment/route limits are a thing.

maria: yes. soft limits: route table entries and peering counts. one mitigation is bucketing tenants into a small set of regional TGWs by scale tier. another is ephemeral overlay to reduce aws route pressure.

sam: overlay (wireguard/ebpf mesh) reduces route bloat but adds ops complexity and throughput ceiling. also makes cost attribution harder.

kevin: what about identity/certs? do we terminate mTLS at the agent in the customer VPC?

tess: my suggestion: terminate control-plane mTLS at an agent sidecar inside the customer VPC for edge-demarc. that keeps private keys and trust roots local and satisfies air-gapped customers. fallback to central relay for agentless onboarding.

maria: agent approach requires a careful upgrade/rollback plan and a minimal footprint. for provider-owned VPCs we can manage the agent lifecycle; for customer-owned VPCs we need onboarding manifest + trust bundle.

sam: can we keep data-plane (heavy model traffic) consolidated to regional egress gateways while control-plane auth remains at edge? split-plane approach seems promising: identity isolation + throughput efficiency.

kevin: agree. two operational must-haves to include in the RFC: 1) a stable customer-facing egress IP option (either preserve source IP via agent or provide per-tenant static NAT ranges customers can whitelist) and 2) automated route-table lifecycle management to prevent quiet route leaks.

tess: for egress IPs we can offer a knob: agent-preserve-srcip OR regional-static-nat with tenant-specific elastic IP pool. include terraform example in appendix.

maria: automation notes: incremental, idempotent routing apply; GC job to remove stale routes after TTL; alerts when route table entries grow above threshold. also audit tags to backfill ownership.

sam: monitoring requirements: per-tenant control-plane latency SLO, peering attach health, NAT pool utilization, and route-churn metrics.

infra-bot: created INFRA-9243 to track automation work: route GC, NAT allocator, and peering-threshold alerts.

kevin: outstanding for RFC: cost model sketch for regionals vs TGW, expected scale limits, and a runbook for peering exhaustion and shard cutover.

tess: i'll draft RFC with migration appendix: canary cutover steps, rollback criteria, and cost comparison. will post by EOD Friday. thanks all :rocket:
